## Teaching points

1. Left lower quadrant pain is not always diverticulitis: left-sided appendicitis occurs with midgut malrotation or nonrotation and with situs inversus, and most of these patients present with left lower quadrant pain.
2. Contrast-enhanced CT shows both the inflamed appendix and the anatomy: a left-sided colon, right-sided small bowel and an abnormal SMA–SMV relationship (normally the SMV lies to the right of the SMA).
3. Situs inversus mirrors all the viscera (liver, spleen, heart); in nonrotation only the bowel is misplaced.
4. Knowing the anatomy before surgery guides the approach; here the appendix was removed through a midline incision rather than a right iliac fossa incision.
5. Rotation anomalies can cause midgut volvulus; fever, tachycardia and peritonitis around day 3 after appendectomy suggest a stump leak or abscess and call for repeat CT.
